data.title: Carlyle CEO Harvey Schwartz Says the Fed Is Unlikely to Raise Rates Repeatedly
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Carlyle Group CEO Harvey Schwartz said the Federal Reserve is unlikely to raise rates repeatedly even though markets appear to have priced in rate-hike expectations, and he said U.S. economic data remain strong despite conflicts in Europe and Iran and persistent inflation. Schwartz said on Tuesday that the Federal Reserve is expected to keep watching economic data, adding that markets clearly expect rate hikes but it does not feel like the economy is entering a rate-hike cycle or a sharp rate-cut cycle.

data.title: Wall Street Calls: Rosenblatt Starts Nokia at Buy, Guggenheim Lifts New York Times to Buy
data.description: According to CNBC, Rosenblatt initiated coverage of Nokia with a buy rating and called the company a powerhouse, saying its Network Infrastructure segment is becoming one of the best-positioned optical assets in the AI buildout. Guggenheim upgraded The New York Times Company to buy from neutral and raised its price target to $82 from $70, while Bernstein upgraded Agilon to outperform from market perform and lifted its target to $125 from $86. Other moves included Jefferies initiating Janus Living at buy, Citizens upgrading Radiant Logistics to market outperform from market perform with a $10 price target, and Oppenheimer initiating Vishay Intertechnology at outperform with a $42 price target. Guggenheim also initiated Northrop Grumman at buy, Cantor Fitzgerald started Bentley Systems at overweight, Wells Fargo upgraded Ulta to equal weight from underweight, and Canaccord initiated Einride at buy. Additional calls included Cantor starting Samsara at overweight, Compass Point initiating Hyperliquid Strategies at buy, Berenberg upgrading Eli Lilly to buy from hold, RBC upgrading ResMed to outperform from sector perform, JPMorgan initiating Dave at overweight, Oppenheimer upgrading Etsy to outperform from market perform, and JPMorgan upgrading Adient and Middleby to overweight from neutral. Bank of America reiterated buy ratings on Nvidia, Marvell and Advanced Micro Devices, William Blair upgraded SEI Investments to outperform from market perform, Evercore ISI reiterated outperform on Apple, JPMorgan reiterated overweight on Amazon, and UBS reiterated buy on Palantir while raising its price target to $250 from $220.

data.title: Market News | Four Pressures Converge on Equities With the Fed Decision a Day Away
data.description: European stocks opened broadly lower again, with selling in Italy particularly heavy and the overall backdrop firmly risk-off.Brent crude traded above $107 a barrel after another attack on Saudi energy infrastructure this week sparked fresh supply concerns. The 10-year US Treasury yield rose above 5.02%, its highest since October 2023.US futures pointed lower, with S&P 500 futures down about 0.4% and Nasdaq futures 0.3% after Wall Street was led lower by technology stocks.No Single Variable Explains ItThe distinguishing feature of this session is that nothing in particular went wrong.Oil above $100, Treasury yields above 5%, a more hawkish Fed outlook and lingering AI uncertainty are each individually manageable. Arriving together, they remove the offsets that normally cushion any one of them.An energy shock usually coincides with growth expectations that support earnings. Rising yields usually accompany an expanding economy. AI weakness usually occurs against a supportive rate backdrop.None of those offsets is currently available, and that is what separates a broad decline from a rotation.Italian Banks Are the Specific Weak PointItaly's benchmark index led the decline after a sharp selloff the previous session, with bank stocks especially under pressure again.That concentration is not incidental. Italian banks carry substantial sovereign debt on their balance sheets, which makes them the most direct equity expression of European long-end yield moves.Long-dated sovereign yields have hit multi-decade highs simultaneously across the US, Japan, Germany and France. The ECB raised its deposit rate to 2.5% last week while lifting its 2027 and 2028 inflation outlook, with Deutsche Bank's Mark Wall saying another December move now looks "more likely than not."A bank holding government paper at pre-repricing prices faces mark-to-market pressure that has nothing to do with its lending book.Yesterday's selloff also hit technology names, with Prysmian and STMicroelectronics among those affected.The Long End Is Doing More Damage Than the Policy RateWednesday's decision addresses overnight funding. The move pressuring equities is happening further out the curve.The 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.40%, its highest since June 2007. The 10-year rose 6.2 basis points to 5.021%, outpacing the two-year's 4.4 basis point move to 4.676% — a steepening that reverses the flattening Friday's CPI produced.ING rate strategists noted the disconnect: "Logically, a rate hike should have calmed the long end, yet the long end is typically extremely volatile."Mischler Financial's Tom di Galoma attributed the move to rate expectations, increased corporate and government debt supply, growth prospects and concern about the long-term US fiscal path. "Our budget, deficit, and overall debt structure continue to expand," he said.Only the first of those four resolves when a tightening cycle ends.Technology Carries the Most Duration RiskEquities weighted toward cash flows years forward reprice hardest against a rising long end, which is why technology led both sessions.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 5.9% Monday in its worst session since July 1, with the Nasdaq 100 at a six-week low. Nvidia dropped more than 4% while Intel, Micron and SanDisk each fell over 7%.The AI uncertainty di Galoma's list does not cover has its own source. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for the industry to slow development over the weekend, with OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk agreeing — a warning originating with the people whose revenue depends on the pace continuing.Anthropic separately signed a $13.7 billion six-year compute agreement with Rumble the same day.The Oil Constraint Is PhysicalBrent above $107 reflects a supply bottleneck rather than a risk premium.Saudi Arabia closed the East-West pipeline, which runs to the Red Sea port of Yanbu and exists specifically to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. With Hormuz disrupted and the bypass shut, production fell to 6.238 million barrels per day — the lowest since 1990. Bab El-Mandeb has also come under threat, closing the remaining alternative.A risk premium unwinds when tensions ease. An export bottleneck unwinds only when a route reopens.President Trump suggested Monday that the conflict could end soon, and prices dipped before resuming their climb on the latest infrastructure attack.The Fed Cannot Address Most of ThisMarkets price a 25 basis point increase at roughly 87% to 93% depending on venue, with UBS, HSBC, Barclays, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America and JPMorgan all expecting the move.Their paths diverge sharply after it — UBS at 50 basis points this year, Bank of America at 75, Deutsche Bank running through March 2027, and Jefferies expecting fewer than markets price.QCP Capital identified the bind: continued energy prices could keep the Fed restrictive, while economic data weakness caused by those same costs would argue for patience.Bitcoin traded around $77,000 after crossing $79,000 Monday, having reclaimed its 50-week exponential moving average at $77,430 before slipping back. The decision comes Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. ET, alongside updated projections and a Warsh press conference.

data.title: US Official: Iran Tried to Seize Navy Drone Patrolling the Strait of Hormuz
data.description:
A U.S. official said on Monday that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps used boats in an attempt to capture a U.S. Navy unmanned vessel patrolling the Strait of Hormuz. According to Sina Finance, after the attempted seizure was identified, a U.S. drone fired two missiles at the boats and destroyed them, with most people on board killed.

U.S. Central Command spokesman Colonel Tim Hawkins confirmed the failed seizure attempt, saying Iranian small boats had recently tried to take a U.S. unmanned surface vessel and that Central Command responded forcefully. Hawkins said the unmanned surface vessel remained under U.S. operational control.

The incident came as the United States sought to protect rising commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. A U.S. official said tanker traffic through the strait had begun to be arranged for daytime passage with Gulf countries, rather than only at night as in recent months. Another U.S. official said Saudi Arabia had sharply increased the number of tankers passing through the strait as the conflict in the Red Sea and with the Houthis escalated. The U.S. military has also expanded the mine-clearing security zone along the strait's main shipping lane. On average, 40 ships now cross the strait each day under U.S. guidance and protection, and about 14 million barrels of oil are exported through the waterway daily. Over the past week, several tankers carrying liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas also passed through the strait.

data.title: Musk Teases Possible Tesla-SpaceX Combination

Musk made the comment while responding to a question about why Tesla and SpaceX remain separate.

data.title: Market News | Wall Street Is Unanimous on September and Split on Everything After It
data.description: More than a dozen banks expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates 25 basis points on September 16.UBS, HSBC, Barclays, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase have all converged on the call. Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs dropped hold positions to get there.The federal funds target currently sits at 3.50% to 3.75%.The Paths Diverge Immediately AfterConsensus on Wednesday masks substantial disagreement on what follows, and the range is wide enough to matter more than the decision.UBS projects 50 basis points of tightening by year-end. Bank of America sees 75 basis points in 2026. HSBC and Barclays both expect September and December moves. Morgan Stanley forecasts two hikes alongside an ECB move in the near term.Deutsche Bank runs longest, expecting September, December and March 2027.Jefferies sits at the other end, expecting fewer than the roughly 3.5 hikes markets price over the longer term. Global economist Mohit Kumar argued the first move is a credibility matter while subsequent ones depend on how long the war lasts and the trend of oil prices.That spread — from 50 basis points to a cycle extending into 2027 — is what Wednesday's dot plot either resolves or widens. The decision itself is priced. The projections are not.Barclays Shifted After Jackson Hole, Not After CPIThe sequencing of these revisions identifies what actually moved forecasters.Barclays shifted to September and December hikes following Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, weeks before the inflation data arrived.Warsh had said: "We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do."That warning did the work. August's core CPI at 0.3% against a 0.2% consensus confirmed rather than created the case, and PCE inflation running at 3.7% remains the figure Warsh built his argument around.Oil pushing back above $100 a barrel supplied the second input, with Brent at $105 after Saudi Arabia closed the pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.Pompliano Is the Visible DissentBitcoin investor Anthony Pompliano posted that the Federal Reserve "should NOT raise interest rates," drawing substantial public backing.The position is normative rather than predictive — an argument about what the Fed ought to do rather than what it will. But it identifies the case that has largely disappeared from sell-side coverage.An energy-driven inflation impulse is a supply shock, and tightening into a supply shock constrains demand without addressing the cause. QCP Capital framed the same tension: continued energy prices could keep the Fed restrictive, while economic data weakness caused by those costs would argue for patience.Jefferies' framing of the first hike as a credibility measure implicitly concedes the point. A move justified by credibility is not a move justified by the inflation mechanism.Bitcoin Crossed $79,000 and Gave It BackMore than $100 million in shorts were liquidated in 30 minutes as Bitcoin crossed $79,000, after President Trump suggested the Iran conflict could end.Price has since slipped back to about $77,000.Analysts flag $79,500 to $80,000 as the area where selling pressure should build, and Bitcoin has failed at $80,000 repeatedly this month. Glassnode data explains why: nearly 8% of total supply was acquired between $80,000 and $82,000 — the largest concentration at any comparable range — with the US spot ETF cohort's average cost basis in the same band.The liquidation pattern this month has run in both directions. An inflation surprise earlier in September triggered $562 million in liquidations, and Monday's move produced $100 million on the short side.Santiment data shows BTC-denominated open contracts fell 13.5% between September 3 and 11 against a 5% price decline, leaving positioning roughly 20% below pre-rally levels. That limits the cascade available Wednesday in either direction.Two Events Land Within 24 HoursThe FOMC begins its two-day meeting September 15, the same day as the Senate's Clarity Act cloture vote, with the rate decision due September 16.The cloture vote requires 60 votes to advance H.R. 3633 to floor debate — a procedural gate rather than passage. A new draft circulating among lawmakers runs over 600 pages, and Democrats have continued to raise concerns about the absent bipartisan ethics agreement.Markets price the September hike at roughly 87% to 93% depending on venue and timing, up from around 60% at the end of August.The 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.40%, its highest since June 2007, while the 10-year cleared 5% for the first time since October 2023 — with the long end rising faster than the short end into a decision that only addresses the short end.

data.title: AMC and Robinhood Clash Over Tokenized Stock Rights
data.description:
AMC Entertainment Holdings Inc. Chief Executive Officer Adam Aron and Robinhood Markets Inc. co-founder Vlad Tenev are clashing over who can create a tradable version of a public company’s stock, according to Bloomberg.

The dispute comes five years after Aron and Tenev emerged as two of the defining figures of the meme-stock boom.

data.title: Market News | The 30-Year Tops 5.40% and the 10-Year Clears 5% as the Curve Steepens Into the Fed
data.description: The US 30-year Treasury yield rose to an intraday high of 5.40%, its highest level since June 2007.The 10-year cleared 5% for the first time since October 2023 and extended in Asian trading, rising 6.2 basis points to 5.021% per Tradeweb data. The two-year rose 4.4 basis points to 4.676%.Yields rose across all maturities ahead of Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision, with markets pricing a 93% probability of a 25 basis point increase according to London Stock Exchange Group data.The Curve Flipped in Three SessionsThe relationship between the two maturities is the most informative development, and it has reversed.Friday's CPI print produced a flattening. The two-year jumped six basis points to 4.61% while the 10-year held flat at 4.95%. That combination reads as a market treating the Fed's response as sufficient — a central bank seen as behind the curve would push long yields higher alongside short ones, because persistent inflation gets priced into the out years.Tuesday inverted it. The 10-year rose 6.2 basis points against the two-year's 4.4, steepening the curve.The long end leading means the market has stopped treating this as a policy-path story and started treating it as something the policy path does not fix.ING rate strategists identified the expected mechanism and its failure: "Logically, a rate hike should have calmed the long end, yet the long end is typically extremely volatile."Four Forces, Only One of Which Is the FedMischler Financial managing director Tom di Galoma listed what has driven yields higher over the past month: rising hike expectations, increased corporate and government debt supply, optimistic growth prospects, and concern about the long-term US fiscal path."Our budget, deficit, and overall debt structure continue to expand," he said. Friday's inflation acceleration, in his framing, "could be the straw that breaks the camel's back."That composition determines how the level resolves. A yield driven by Fed expectations falls when the tightening cycle ends. A yield driven by supply and fiscal concern does not, because neither is addressed by the policy rate.The 30-year is the maturity least connected to overnight funding, which is why its move to 5.40% carries more signal than the headline 10-year figure. Thirty-year borrowing costs reflect expectations about inflation, fiscal sustainability and the compensation investors require for holding duration across decades.The 2007 Comparison Is the Relevant OneJune 2007 predates the financial crisis, the zero-rate era and every unconventional policy tool deployed since.A 30-year at 5.40% means long-term US borrowing costs have returned to a pre-crisis baseline while the debt stock financed at those costs is several multiples of what it was then. National debt approached $40 trillion in August.Every percentage point on that stock is a materially different number than it was in 2007, and refinancing occurs at whatever the long end demands.The Buyback Program Was Designed to Prevent Exactly ThisTreasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in mid-August that long-dated yields were too high, with the 10-year then at roughly 4.75%, and promised to bring them down through buybacks and jawboning.The most recent operation announced up to $6 billion in purchases, drew $10.5 billion in tenders and accepted $5.2 billion — below its own ceiling. Yields sat near session highs afterward.The 30-year touched a 19-year high in August before that expansion and has now exceeded it.CNBC contributor Oliver Renick named the structural objection: "If Bessent is a buyer of bonds at any price like Saylor is of bitcoin, why would anyone with inventory not sell all the way down?" A buyer publicly committed to purchasing regardless of price removes the incentive to sell early.Stanley Druckenmiller, who mentored both Bessent and Chair Kevin Warsh, told a private audience that Fed members describing policy as restrictive are "just ridiculous," adding that yields "if anything seem a little low."Risk Dimensions CIO Mark Connors framed the sequence: "The market has now challenged both sides of policy. Bessent went first. Even tripling Treasury buybacks hasn't tamed the long end. Now, Warsh, after talking disinflation, is being forced towards higher rates."A Global Repricing, Not a US OneThe move is not isolated to Treasuries.Long-dated sovereign yields have hit multi-decade highs simultaneously across the US, Japan, Germany and France. Japan's 10-year touched 3% this month for the first time in three decades, and its five-year hit a record.Simultaneous long-end repricing across four major sovereign markets is not explicable by any single central bank. It describes investors demanding more compensation to hold government debt generally.Marty Bent summarised the framing behind a chart plotting global bonds against commodities: "The world needs more stuff, not more financialization. You can manipulate the price of money. You can't financial engineer your way out of a shortage of energy and raw materials."The Energy Shock Monetary Policy Cannot ReachBrent traded at $105 and WTI above $100 after Saudi Arabia closed the East-West pipeline, which runs to the Red Sea port of Yanbu and exists to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.With Hormuz disrupted and the bypass shut, Saudi production fell to 6.238 million barrels per day — the lowest since 1990. Bab El-Mandeb has also come under threat, closing the remaining alternative route.QCP Capital identified the resulting policy bind: continued energy prices could keep the Fed restrictive, while economic data weakness caused by those same costs would argue for patience.Jefferies global economist Mohit Kumar drew the conclusion for the path. The first hike may be necessary from a credibility standpoint, but subsequent moves depend on how long the war lasts and the trend of oil prices.The Equity and Crypto TransmissionLong-duration assets reprice hardest against a rising long end.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 5.9% Monday in its worst session since July 1, with the Nasdaq 100 at a six-week low. Nvidia dropped more than 4% while Intel, Micron and SanDisk each fell over 7%.Bitcoin went the other way, rising roughly 3% above $79,000 after President Trump suggested the Iran conflict could end and reclaiming its 50-week exponential moving average at $77,430.QCP had described the setup before the CPI print: "This is the worst mix for Bitcoin: a competing 5% risk-free rate without the nominal-growth impulse that usually accompanies yield moves." That 5% arrived Monday.The offsetting argument rests on why yields are rising. Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with the 10-year sits at −0.17 against gold's −0.41, and when the move reflects fiscal deterioration rather than growth, the investors demanding more compensation for government paper are the same ones seeking assets outside that system.Gold fell 1.2% to $4,296.68 on Monday, a third straight weekly decline, while Bitcoin rose — consistent with that correlation gap.Wednesday Does Not Address the Long EndThe Fed decides Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. ET with updated projections and a Warsh press conference.None of that speaks to the 30-year directly. Markets price roughly 3.5 hikes over the longer term, while Bank of America and RBC Capital Markets both expect 75 basis points this year and Jefferies expects fewer.The dot plot either validates that path or corrects it, and Warsh has to deliver the signal without the forward guidance he rejected at Jackson Hole. The projections provide it impersonally, which may be the intended route.Di Galoma's test applies to both maturities: whether these levels hold is what determines if the economy and equity markets can support them.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Schork Says Iran Is Pressuring Saudi Oil Flows East and West
data.description: Stephen Schork, principal and editor at The Schork Group, said Iran has expanded control over Middle East oil flows and that the US strategic petroleum reserve "will be drawn down, by November, to its operational limits," according to Bloomberg.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Carney Widens Canada’s Investment Tax Write-Off
data.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney is broadening a major investment tax deduction in Canada to cover oil and gas pipelines, mining property and other assets eligible for accelerated write-offs, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: US Mortgage Rates Near 7% as Housing Recovery Hopes Fade
data.description:
U.S. 30-year fixed mortgage rates are nearing 7% for the first time since January 2025. According to Sina Finance, the rise has been driven mainly by the Iran war pushing up Treasury yields, adding pressure to a U.S. housing market already in its fourth year of stagnation.

Freddie Mac data showed the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 6.76% last week, but daily rates have since jumped above 7%. Michael Fratantoni, chief economist at the Mortgage Bankers Association, said the sharp move would prompt potential buyers to pause and could keep them from signing contracts or applying for loans.

Mortgage rates typically track the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield, which briefly topped 5% on September 14 for the first time since late 2023. The Federal Reserve is expected to raise rates on September 16 for the first time in three years.

The National Association of Realtors said existing-home sales fell 2% in August from the previous month to an annualized pace of 3.98 million, the lowest since June last year. Zillow economist Kara Ng said calculations for the rest of this year will be very challenging, after the firm cut its 2026 home-sales growth forecast to 1.3% from 4.3% and now expects a 3.5% decline in the fourth quarter.

Higher mortgage rates are also weighing on new-home construction, as builders offer larger rate buydowns to support sales and face thinner margins.

data.title: Hassett Says Private Sector Can Handle AI Risks, Rejects Government Takeover
data.description: According to CNBC, National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said the private sector is capable of addressing the risks posed by rapidly advancing artificial intelligence and that the government should not expand its role. Speaking on "Squawk Box," Hassett said the issues are solvable and that the private sector is the right place to address them, while adding that the government is still watching closely and can use law enforcement when necessary to ensure firms act responsibly.

data.title: Tom Lee Says AI Debt Concerns Are Rising, Keeps Bullish View on Nvidia and Related Assets
data.description: Tom Lee said concerns are rising over debt financing for AI infrastructure, but he argued that expanding growth industries do not rely entirely on equity capital. He said increased borrowing by AI companies does not mean their business models have failed or that a bubble is about to end badly. According to Odaily, Lee said AI will become the economy's third major growth engine and that investors often underestimate the long-term value and adoption speed of new technologies in their early stages. He said he remains positive on Nvidia, semiconductors, memory chips, and energy and power assets driven by expanding computing demand.

data.title: Samson Mow Says Blockstream Could Offer Bounty After Hacker Returns Stolen Funds
data.description: Bitcoin News posted on X that Samson Mow said Blockstream’s refusal to pay a ransom does not rule out offering a bounty if the hacker returns the remaining stolen funds. According to Odaily, Mow said the stolen funds belong to Liquid users, so Blockstream cannot negotiate over them, and any bounty would need to be handled as a separate and reasonable arrangement.

data.title: Hutchison Telecom Macau To End Mobile Services On December 1
data.description:
Macau Post and Telecommunications Bureau said it received an application from Hutchison Telephone (Macau), a unit of CK Hutchison Holdings, to give up its 4G mobile telecom licence and plans to end mobile communications services in Macau from December 1, according to Ming Pao.

The bureau said the move was a commercial decision made by the company based on its own operating conditions. To protect users' interests, it has asked Hutchison to draw up a complete transition plan and said it will closely supervise the exit process in accordance with the law to ensure a smooth handover of services.

data.title: GM Restores Apple CarPlay in Latest Infotainment System
data.description: General Motors Co. is integrating Apple Inc.’s CarPlay into its latest infotainment system, three years after removing the interface from its electric vehicles and upsetting some consumers, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Company Plans Perpetual Preferred Share Offering Under MORE Ticker
data.description:
The company plans to issue perpetual preferred shares under the ticker MORE, targeting to raise 15 million to 25 million pounds, with a minimum fundraising size of 10 million pounds. According to Odaily, the shares will require support from three market makers for listing admission.

Holders will receive cumulative weekly dividends and liquidation priority, but no voting rights, and the company may redeem the shares. By mid-2026, SWC held 2,878 bitcoins, and after a capital reduction approved by the High Court, the company had 132.5 million pounds in distributable reserves available for payment.

data.title: JD Sports Appoints New North America CEO and Chief Marketing Officer
data.description: JD Sports Fashion Plc named new executives to lead North America and marketing as the sports retailer seeks to reverse soft sales and a prolonged stock-market slump, according to Bloomberg.
